headline: Microsoft closed an actively exploited Outlook zero-day among nearly 1,100 fixes while SAP patched four maximum-severity flaws and attackers hijacked the Xen Orchestra, Barracuda, and N-able consoles that administer everything else.

emerging_trends.text: Microsoft's November Patch Tuesday ran past 1,200 fixes, SAP closed four flaws scored 10.0, and Adobe shipped 110 more, a volume that forces defenders to triage by evidence of exploitation rather than by count.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Microsoft Patches an Exploited Outlook Zero-Day

emerging_trends.text: Attackers spent the day inside administrative software itself—the Xen Orchestra console that runs XCP-ng hypervisors, N-able's N-central platform for managed service providers, and Barracuda's email gateways—where one authentication bypass reaches every machine underneath.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Xen Orchestra Bypass Hands Over Virtualization Hosts

emerging_trends.text: Railway's $740,000 in fraudulent AI usage, Qubole's stolen Amazon Web Services credentials, and the widening Fireworks AI intrusion show attackers treating cloud providers as a single door into every customer behind them, with the victim's model budget as the payoff.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Qubole Credentials Open More Than a Dozen Clouds

topics.title: Microsoft Patches an Exploited Outlook Zero-Day
topics.latest_developments: Microsoft fixed nearly 1,100 vulnerabilities on November 10, 2026, its second four-digit patch month in a row, among them CVE-2026-124194, a Microsoft Outlook zero-day the company says attackers already exploit, and 63 critical flaws; BleepingComputer counted 1,235 fixes once the Chromium updates for Microsoft Edge come in.
topics.summary: The critical set reaches Microsoft Exchange, SharePoint, Windows Search, and LDAP, so administrators should install the Outlook fix first and work down that list. Adobe, Apple, Google, and Mozilla all shipped security updates the same week, which leaves patching teams a crowded queue.

topics.title: SAP Patches Four Perfect-Score Flaws
topics.latest_developments: SAP's Security Patch Day on November 10, 2026 closed four vulnerabilities the vendor rates 10.0, the maximum CVSS score, three in the NetWeaver application server and one in the Web Dispatcher, and SecurityWeek named the two worst ICM2SHELL and ProxyGate inside a release of 42 advisories, nine of them critical, covering 35 vulnerabilities across NetWeaver, Web Dispatcher, and Gateway.
topics.summary: NetWeaver is the application server nearly every SAP installation runs on, and the Web Dispatcher sits in front of it taking web requests off the internet. The SANS Internet Storm Center logged honeypot probes on November 9, 2026 hunting for SAP NetWeaver webshells, so administrators should apply the patches immediately and hunt for shells already dropped.

topics.title: Barracuda Gateways and N-able Fall to Public Exploits
topics.latest_developments: CISA added six actively exploited flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on November 10, 2026, among them both Barracuda Email Security Gateway bugs that Barracuda confirmed attackers now chain for root—CVE-2026-116606, an authorization bypass, and CVE-2026-111560, an operating system command injection—plus CVE-2026-20320, an XML external entity flaw in Cisco BroadWorks, and CVE-2026-111793 in Openwave Messaging's Webtop media transcoder; N-able put the N-central disclosure at 33 zero-days with working proof-of-concept exploits, a set the researcher calls Able2Shell.
topics.summary: The Barracuda chain hands an attacker with no login full control of the appliance that filters a company's email; watchTowr published the working steps on November 5, 2026. N-able keeps its hosted N-central environments offline and tells on-premises customers to shut their own servers down, because the Able2Shell bugs allow remote code execution, credential theft, and the creation of administrator accounts.

topics.title: Xen Orchestra Bypass Hands Over Virtualization Hosts
topics.latest_developments: Vates VMS, the French company behind Xen Orchestra, tracks the exploited authentication bypass as VSA-2026-062 with no CVE identifier yet and pinned it on REST cookie parsing that turns the string authenticationToken=j:%7B%7D into an empty object the authentication check then accepts, handing attackers administrator privileges over XCP-ng virtualization hosts.
topics.summary: Xen Orchestra administers every virtual machine running on an XCP-ng host, so one bypass reaches the whole fleet; operators should update at once and take the console off the internet. Huntress separately detailed an October 2026 campaign that chained CVE-2026-105133 and CVE-2026-105134 in AhsayCBS backup software to bypass authentication, run arbitrary commands, and plant a sandbox-evading Python implant.

topics.title: Chrome XML Zero-Day and iMessage Eavesdropping
topics.latest_developments: Google shipped emergency Chrome updates for CVE-2026-125350, a high-severity use-after-free in the browser's XML component that an anonymous reporter flagged on November 6, 2026 and that attackers already exploit, the eighth exploited Chrome zero-day of 2026, and Apple fixed an iMessage flaw that lets a remote attacker join a group chat and read its traffic.
topics.summary: The Chrome release carries nine fixes in all; users should restart the browser to take them. Apple's updates also close a second iMessage flaw that shows a newly added member the messages sent before they joined, patch Bluetooth pairing bugs, and extend to the iPhone XS, XS Max, and XR and the seventh-generation iPad.

topics.title: Turla's Cereal Toolset Siphons Government Email
topics.latest_developments: ESET disclosed on November 10, 2026 that Turla, the Russia-aligned group also tracked as Snake, planted a previously undocumented modular .NET toolset researchers named Cereal on the Microsoft Exchange servers of two government organizations, one in Kazakhstan and one in Romania, and copied selected messages straight out of the mail flow, among them correspondence those governments exchanged with NATO and European Union officials.
topics.summary: Cereal needs no attacker-owned command server: operators send instructions to the victim's own internet-facing Exchange server disguised as ordinary Outlook Web Access, Autodiscover, and ActiveSync requests, which leaves little outbound traffic to spot. Exchange administrators at government bodies should audit server-side modules and inspect those three request paths for anomalies.

topics.title: Qubole Credentials Open More Than a Dozen Clouds
topics.latest_developments: Railway said on November 10, 2026 that attackers exploited flaws in its hosting infrastructure, stole customer authentication secrets, and ran roughly $740,000 in fraudulent AI usage, with credentials for as many as 100,000 workspaces exposed, the same day SecurityWeek reported that the attacker holding Qubole's identity and access management credentials reached more than a dozen organizations' Amazon Web Services accounts and took files, secrets, keys, environment variables, and credentials.
topics.summary: Qubole, the data lake platform Idera owns, holds standing access into its customers' AWS accounts, which turned one credential theft into break-ins across the customer base between October 14 and October 26, 2026. Fireworks AI said on Monday, November 9, 2026 that the intrusion it first disclosed October 10, 2026 also reached account and billing information, secrets, datasets, and incomplete model weights for a limited set of accounts; customers of all three providers should rotate every reachable secret and review cloud audit logs for October.

topics.title: France Summons Iran's Ambassador Over Refrigeration Sabotage
topics.latest_developments: France summoned the Iranian ambassador and said it will seek European sanctions against the people behind the October 2026 refrigeration attacks, a day after blaming Shahid Kaveh, a cyber unit of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.
topics.summary: The attackers reached refrigeration controllers at roughly 700 French retail sites on the night of October 11, 2026 and raised defrost settings to high temperatures, spoiling food and starting at least 15 fires. Investigators had previously tied the same unit to attacks on industrial controllers at United States water utilities; operators of cold chain and building control systems should pull those controllers off the open internet.

topics.title: Claude 5.2 Tops an Offensive AI Benchmark
topics.latest_developments: Dark Reading reported on November 10, 2026 that forks of ARTEX, the open-source AI penetration-testing framework, along with 45 similar tools, still run credential attacks and cloud break-ins at machine speed across multiple industries, a day after Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2, whose Fable version outscored OpenAI's GPT-6 Cyber on a multi-stage cyberattack benchmark while its safety classifiers refuse high-risk work such as penetration testing and exploit generation and serve an Opus 4.8 answer instead.
topics.summary: The release puts a broadly available commercial model at the front of measured offensive capability, with policy classifiers rather than weaker skills doing the restraining. Acronis's Threat Research Unit counted more than 575 malicious OpenClaw skills that delivered malware to Windows and macOS machines, and traced an investigation it calls BOSSAI to one operator who wired more than 10 AI models to reconnaissance, scanning, and exploitation tools and coordinated the work over WeChat and LINE.

topics.title: Unpatched iOS Sandbox Escape Risks Wallet Keys
topics.latest_developments: Binance warned on November 10, 2026 that worse_query, an iOS sandbox escape a researcher who goes by forcequit published on GitHub on Sunday, November 8, 2026, lets one app read other apps' private files on iPhones running iOS 26 and 27, including versions 26.7.1, 27.0.1, and 27.2, and Apple's November 9, 2026 updates list no fix for it.
topics.summary: The escape puts the seed phrases, private keys, and login credentials that wallet and banking apps store on a phone within reach of any malicious app a person installs. Until Apple ships a fix, iOS 26 and 27 users should install no unfamiliar apps and keep large cryptocurrency balances off the device.

business_politics.title: Wachtell Takes Over the Nvidia Espionage Probe
business_politics.latest_developments: Nvidia retained Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz and a former acting United States attorney for the Southern District of New York to run the board's investigation into whether a foreign intelligence effort targeted Chief Executive Jensen Huang, and the Financial Times reported Tuesday, November 10, that the Commerce Department has delayed adding Megaspeed, the company connected to the alleged Chinese agent, to its trade blacklist as Nvidia shares fell further.
business_politics.summary: American intelligence officials told Huang that the executive he carried on an affair with worked as an agent for China, and Nvidia's board opened a formal inquiry on November 8 while saying it has no reason to believe the chipmaker's secrets or national security suffered. Nvidia supplies the accelerators behind nearly every large artificial-intelligence buildout, so its governance and its chief executive's refusal to groom a successor sit on every equity and credit book exposed to the trade.

business_politics.title: The House Moves on Hegseth's Impeachment
business_politics.latest_developments: Republican leaders blocked Representative Thomas Massie's impeachment resolutions against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth on the House floor Tuesday evening, November 10, and Democrats say they will revive the effort when they take control of Congress in January; House Republicans the same day elected Representative Jim Jordan of Ohio their leader for the next Congress over Steve Scalise, and Senate Republicans reelected John Thune of South Dakota.
business_politics.summary: Hegseth used his first Pentagon press conference in six months to call the impeachment push a "political spectacle" built on "policy disagreements" and to defend his conduct of the Iran war, which Republicans blame for their losses of November 3 that handed both chambers to Democrats. The Wall Street Journal reports that the impeachment hands bruised Capitol Hill Republicans leverage over the White House, and the defense secretary's survival now tracks the course of a war President Trump says he wants to settle.

business_politics.title: Waller Floats a Half-Point Fed Increase
business_politics.latest_developments: United States stocks closed lower Tuesday, November 10, after October consumer prices rose 0.4% from September against the 0.3% economists expected: two-year Treasury yields jumped the most since 2024, the 10-year passed 5%, the WSJ Dollar Index rose 0.49% to 97.54, and gold settled 2.1% lower with silver down 2.8%, while Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said he leans toward a quarter-point increase and told the Financial Times he would weigh a half-point move, the largest since 2022, if inflation refuses to slow.
business_politics.summary: Traders have now firmed up bets on a Federal Reserve increase in December, a step that reprices mortgages, leveraged credit, and every rate-sensitive book on Wall Street. The 0.4% monthly pace slowed from September's 0.6%, and last year's government shutdown interrupted data collection, which complicates the comparison; Bank of England Deputy Governor Clare Lombardelli signaled the same morning that London will likely raise its key rate again soon.

business_politics.title: Anthropic Trims Its IPO Target to $1.3 Trillion
business_politics.latest_developments: CoreWeave met Wall Street expectations Tuesday, November 10, reported a business backlog of $133 billion, and lined up a multibillion-dollar debt deal backed by its chips and customer prepayments; OpenAI reported revenue of $10 billion with heavy continuing losses, and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission postponed the exchanges' push to list artificial-intelligence computing futures over price-manipulation concerns.
business_politics.summary: The Claude maker now seeks a valuation of $1.3 trillion to $1.4 trillion and as much as $64 billion of proceeds, roughly $200 billion below the figure it insisted on last week, in a debut it has promised before Thanksgiving; its seven insiders will each sell about $250 million of stock, keep total voting control, and hold stakes worth roughly $18 billion apiece. Goldman Sachs told clients it expects Anthropic revenue above $600 billion and positive cash flow by 2030, while SoftBank Group swung to a quarterly loss of about $7 billion on charges tied to power-generating equipment for United States data centers.

business_politics.title: Brent Falls Below $90 as Trump Steps Back From Iran
business_politics.latest_developments: Oil futures settled lower again Tuesday, November 10, after President Trump repeated that the United States does not expect to renew attacks on Iran while talks progress, and the absence of any breakthrough limited the decline; United States natural gas futures settled higher on a cold spell forecast for the eastern United States this weekend.
business_politics.summary: Brent's break below $90 a barrel, its first since August, lifted European and Asian equities, and a consortium of climate scientists now expects global carbon dioxide emissions to fall this year because the war has cut fossil-fuel use. The Wall Street Journal reports that American and Iranian forces have struck islands inside the Strait of Hormuz in a fight for control of the waterway, and the United States Air Force pulled refueling tankers from a second base in eastern England over an Iranian threat.

business_politics.title: Washington Reopens the War Talks and Europe's Security Order
business_politics.latest_developments: United States, Russian, and Ukrainian delegations resumed negotiations on ending the war Tuesday, November 10, and American officials told European capitals that work on a Ukraine ceasefire must run alongside talks about Europe's future security arrangements, an overture to Moscow that alarmed allies.
business_politics.summary: The Financial Times reports low expectations of a breakthrough because Vladimir Putin shows no sign of wanting to halt the fighting, which continues against Ukraine's power grid and the bridges over the Dnipro river. Linking a ceasefire to a rewrite of European security architecture hands the Kremlin the agenda NATO governments have refused to open since 2022, and it lands days after German Chancellor Friedrich Merz threatened to hold up the European Union budget over funding for Kyiv.

business_politics.title: China's Trade Surplus Passes $1 Trillion
business_politics.latest_developments: Chinese customs data released Tuesday, November 10, put the country's trade surplus above $1 trillion for the first ten months of 2026, a pace that sets up an annual record.
business_politics.summary: The surplus lands while Washington presses Beijing to deliver the rare earths and other critical products it committed to in the Busan agreement, and it strengthens the case trading partners make for rebalancing. The Wall Street Journal reports that Chinese officials who read President Trump as weakened by the November 3 midterm losses may instead meet a tougher negotiator.

business.title: Breeze Sells Out Its First Latrobe Flights
business.latest_developments: WTAE and KDKA reported Tuesday, November 10, that Breeze Airways has sold out the first three flights from Arnold Palmer Regional Airport near Latrobe and that the airport is moving to rehire workers it laid off and to staff up for the new service.
business.summary: Arnold Palmer Regional Airport, the Westmoreland County field that lost commercial service and cut jobs, now has a carrier again in Breeze Airways, the low-fare airline that flies point-to-point routes from small airports. The sold-out opening flights give the airport the demand case it needs to restore ground and customer-service positions.

business.title: Downtown Apartments Fill as Office Conversions Stall
business.latest_developments: TribLive reported Tuesday, November 10, that apartments in Pittsburgh's Golden Triangle keep filling up, and that data from the Pittsburgh Downtown Partnership points to real obstacles in turning more office towers into housing.
business.summary: Downtown Pittsburgh's residential demand now outruns its supply, and the city's plan to add residents depends on converting office floors emptied since 2020. The physical and financial hurdles in those buildings set the pace at which the Golden Triangle can add units.

sources.title: Downtown Pittsburgh housing demand is growing, but turning offices into apartments remains a challenge

business.title: Agility Robotics Will Double Its Pittsburgh Workforce
business.latest_developments: An Agility Robotics executive told WPXI Tuesday, November 10, that the humanoid robot maker will double its Pittsburgh workforce now that the company trades on the Nasdaq.
business.summary: Agility Robotics builds the Digit humanoid for warehouse and logistics work and runs a Pittsburgh engineering operation alongside its Oregon base. The hiring plan follows its Wall Street debut last week and puts the company among the largest robotics employers in a city whose robotics sector grew out of Carnegie Mellon University.

sources.title: Agility Robotics exec talks plans to double Pittsburgh workforce after Nasdaq debut

business.title: CMU and Pitt Want the Compute the Region Keeps Rejecting
business.latest_developments: PublicSource reported Tuesday, November 10, that Carnegie Mellon University and the University of Pittsburgh have built their research strategies around artificial intelligence and want local computing capacity, even as municipality after municipality in the region moves to block or pause data centers.
business.summary: Brian Regli, a consultant for the firm proposing a data center in Springdale Borough, told PublicSource that companies spun out of Carnegie Mellon "could do really fantastic things if they had access to the compute and if that compute was readily available within the community." Buffalo Township in Butler County already imposed a data-center moratorium while it writes an ordinance, and other Allegheny Valley communities are weighing the same step.

sources.title: CMU, Pitt embrace AI as region debates data centers

business.title: Walmart Pays $7.8 Million in a Pennsylvania Child-Labor Case
business.latest_developments: Governor Josh Shapiro's administration announced Monday night, November 9, that Walmart will pay nearly $7.8 million to settle what state investigators called systemic child-labor violations, a record settlement for Pennsylvania.
business.summary: Pennsylvania's investigation found violations of the state's child-labor law across Walmart's operations in the commonwealth, where the retailer runs more than a hundred stores and employs tens of thousands of workers. The dollar figure exceeds any previous child-labor settlement the state has secured.

business.title: Keystone and Conemaugh Coal Plants Get an Extension
business.latest_developments: TribLive reported Tuesday, November 10, that the Trump administration's Environmental Protection Agency and Pennsylvania regulators granted an extension to the owners of the Keystone and Conemaugh coal-fired power plants.
business.summary: Keystone, in Armstrong County, and Conemaugh, in Indiana County, rank among the last large coal-burning generators in Western Pennsylvania, and each employs hundreds of workers while anchoring the tax base of its host township. The extension keeps both units running past the compliance deadline their owners faced.

business.title: DiCarlo's Pizza Returns in Brookline
business.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported Tuesday, November 10, that DiCarlo's Pizza plans a return to Pittsburgh with a location in Brookline.
business.summary: DiCarlo's sells Ohio Valley-style square-cut pizza, cheese dropped on the crust after it leaves the oven, and the Brookline storefront puts the chain back inside the city on a South Hills business district that has filled vacancies with independent food operators.

sources.title: DiCarlo's Pizza plots return to Pittsburgh with a Brookline location

business.title: Veterans Hit Walls in the Civilian Job Market
business.latest_developments: TribLive published Tuesday, November 10, the day before Veterans Day, an account of how veterans in the Alle-Kiski Valley struggle to turn military service into civilian employment, built around Chuck Balog of the Army.
business.summary: Balog spent six years as a field artillery officer and helped liberate Kuwait during Operation Desert Storm before he entered the civilian workforce. Employers across Western Pennsylvania court veterans for discipline and technical training, and the gap sits in translating military roles and credentials into job descriptions that hiring managers recognize.

sources.title: Veterans face hurdles transitioning to civilian workforce

business.title: A Turkish Immigrant's Pizza Bar in Sharpsburg
business.latest_developments: TribLive profiled Gino Bros. Pizza Bar in Sharpsburg on Tuesday, November 10, and reported the same morning that a twice-closed pizza shop in O'Hara Township will reopen under new ownership.
business.summary: Ferdi Baylassin left Eskisehir, Turkey, at 21 and now runs Gino Bros. Pizza Bar along the Allegheny River in Sharpsburg, the Allegheny County borough beside Aspinwall. around_town.title: Deluzio Ties ICE Arrests to Local Police
around_town.latest_developments: Representative Chris Deluzio of Aspinwall released a report Tuesday, November 10, finding that local law enforcement helped federal agents make more than half the immigration arrests in his congressional district, and he called for an investigation into which agencies operate outside their jurisdictions; PublicSource traced a surge of detentions in Beaver County to 287(g) agreements between police there and Immigration and Customs Enforcement.
around_town.summary: The federal 287(g) program deputizes local officers to carry out immigration enforcement, and Deluzio's district covers Beaver County and parts of Allegheny County. His office's tally puts a district-level number on how much the arrest total depends on cooperation from municipal and county departments.

around_town.title: Etna Weighs a 32% Tax Increase
around_town.latest_developments: TribLive reported Tuesday, November 10, that Etna council may still need a 32% property tax increase next year even after cuts that include delaying repair of a sewer line and having council members hand-deliver the borough newsletter to avoid postage.
around_town.summary: Etna, the Allegheny County borough on the north bank of the Allegheny River beside Sharpsburg, has run out of easy spending to trim, which leaves the millage rate as the lever council holds before it adopts a 2027 budget.

around_town.title: Council's Budget Director Calls the 2027 Plan Honest
around_town.latest_developments: Pittsburgh City Council Budget Director Kiersten Walmsley told council Tuesday, November 10, that Mayor Corey O'Connor's proposed 2027 budget paints an accurate portrait of the city's finances, however unpretty that portrait looks.
around_town.summary: O'Connor presented his first budget Monday, November 9: no tax increase, millions of dollars of spending cuts against a projected $250 million deficit over five years, and $27 million drawn from the city's reserve fund. Residents packed the council chamber to protest the cuts, and council now works through the plan toward a vote.

sources.title: Pittsburgh's 2027 budget deemed ugly but honest

around_town.summary: Tuesday afternoon reached the low 60s around Pittsburgh under sun and a breeze, the week's warmest stretch. Colder air arriving behind Thursday's system turns the weekend's precipitation to a mix across Western Pennsylvania.

around_town.title: A 38-Foot Spruce Comes to Grant Street
around_town.latest_developments: WPXI reported Tuesday, November 10, that crews will install a 38-foot blue spruce at the City-County Building downtown, closing lanes on Grant Street and nearby routes and snarling traffic through the weekend.
around_town.summary: The tree outside the City-County Building at 414 Grant Street anchors Pittsburgh's holiday display ahead of the 65th Light Up Night on Saturday, November 21. Drivers heading into downtown along Grant Street should expect rolling closures until the installation finishes.

around_town.title: Troopers Find Skill Games Almost Entirely Gone
around_town.latest_developments: The Pennsylvania State Police reported Tuesday, November 10, that troopers visited more than 12,000 establishments under the commonwealth's new skill game enforcement and seized only 14 machines, compliance the agency called nearly 100% successful.
around_town.summary: Skill games sat for years in Pennsylvania bars, social clubs, and convenience stores while the legislature argued over how to treat them, and the new enforcement effort tests whether operators pulled noncompliant machines on their own. The sweep's near-total compliance rate undercuts predictions of a drawn-out fight between troopers and small operators.

sources.title: Compliance with Pennsylvania's new skill game enforcement was nearly 100% successful, state police say

around_town.title: Hempfield Area Delays Its Weapon Detection Rollout
around_town.latest_developments: CurvePoint Chief Executive Skip Smith told TribLive Tuesday, November 10, that Hempfield Area High School has pushed back the formal launch of its artificial-intelligence weapon detection system while his company works through environmental problems with the technology.
around_town.summary: Hempfield Area School District, the Westmoreland County district west of Greensburg, bought the CurvePoint system to scan for weapons at the high school's entrances. Districts across Pennsylvania have spent security money on similar detection systems, and the delay shows how the hardware performs against weather, lighting, and foot traffic in a real building.

sources.title: Hempfield Area delays launch of novel weapon detection system, tech company says

around_town.title: Murrysville and Export Hold Taxes Flat
around_town.latest_developments: Lower Burrell released a proposed 2027 budget with no tax increase Tuesday, November 10, and a Greensburg councilman faulted that city's proposed $14 million budget, which also holds property taxes flat, for a lack of foresight; Murrysville and Export, neighboring Westmoreland County municipalities, each proposed budgets without an increase a day earlier, Murrysville's $12.9 million plan keeping the property tax at 12.15 mills.
around_town.summary: The four sit east of Pittsburgh along the Route 22 and Allegheny River corridors, and each council will take public comment before adopting a final budget in December. Separately, South Greensburg voters approved cutting that borough's council from seven members to five in unofficial results from the November 3 election.

around_town.title: Deer Crashes Climb Across Western Pennsylvania
around_town.latest_developments: PennDOT told KDKA Tuesday, November 10, that vehicle collisions with deer across Western Pennsylvania are rising, and that the agency posts deer crossing signs on specific highway stretches because the animals cross there; WTAE reported the same day that Oakmont Borough's deer management program, which allows archers in borough parks, starts Thursday, November 12, over objections from some residents.
around_town.summary: November's rut and the shift off daylight saving time put more deer on the road during the Pittsburgh region's commuting hours, and PennDOT urges drivers to slow down through marked stretches and to expect a second and third animal behind the first. Oakmont residents split over the archery program, some questioning the need for it and others pointing to overpopulation.

around_town.title: Pittsburgh's Leverage in the New Harrisburg
around_town.latest_developments: Post-Gazette columnist Brandon McGinley handicapped Tuesday, November 10, how much Pittsburgh can extract from a Harrisburg that Democrats now control outright, and pointed to Senator Jay Costa of Forest Hills, the Allegheny County Democrat who leads his caucus.
around_town.summary: Democrats held the Pennsylvania House, took a majority in the state Senate, and reelected Governor Josh Shapiro on November 3, the party's first trifecta in more than 30 years. Allegheny County's delegation now sits inside the majority in both chambers, which puts city priorities such as transit funding and economic development money within reach of a floor vote.

around_town.title: The District Attorney Closes The Linx
around_town.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported Tuesday, November 10, that a third South Side bar now faces closure by the Allegheny County District Attorney's Nuisance Bar Task Force, which shut The Linx until further notice Monday night, November 9, days after closing Capo's.
around_town.summary: The task force counted 28 incidents tied to The Linx, including a false robbery report, in building its case to pull the bar's operations. The closures hit the East Carson Street nightlife corridor, where District Attorney's office prosecutors have made nuisance enforcement their lever over late-night operators.

events.summary: The group formed around the Western Pennsylvania wedding cookie table, the regional custom of stacking a reception with homemade cookies baked by family and friends, and it already holds the record it now aims to beat. around_teams.title: The Steelers Stand Pat at the Deadline
around_teams.latest_developments: The NFL trade deadline passed Tuesday, November 10, with Pittsburgh making no deals, and inside linebacker Patrick Queen and Max Iheanachor met the media the same afternoon as the team came back from its bye.
around_teams.summary: The Post-Gazette reported that the Steelers, who had shopped for depth rather than a headline addition, let the deadline go by and will carry the roster they had through the open week into Sunday night at Cincinnati. Matt Williamson and Wes Uhler spent Tuesday's SNR Drive on deadline day and on the expanded 24-team College Football Playoff, and Queen said he followed the day's trades on his phone like any other fan.

team_usa.title: Manchester United Closes In on Pochettino
team_usa.latest_developments: Sources told ESPN Tuesday night, November 10, that United States men's national team head coach Mauricio Pochettino would welcome a return to the Premier League with Manchester United, whose executives met minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe this week to settle Michael Carrick's future, and ESPN laid out the trade-offs between the two jobs; United States left back Antonee Robinson said the national team's players pay the speculation no mind.
team_usa.summary: Pochettino is preparing the Americans for their Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal against Haiti later this month, a window already thinned by Gio Reyna's injury at Strasbourg. ESPN traces United's worst league position in 40 years and its relegation fight to Ratcliffe's choice of inexperienced backroom appointments, and argues Carrick's stoppage-time rescue of a 4-4 draw at Aston Villa should not save his job.

team_usa.title: Reyna's Strasbourg Revival Stops Again
team_usa.latest_developments: ESPN laid out Tuesday, November 10, how much Gio Reyna had rebuilt at Strasbourg—fit, starting, and scoring—before the injury that pulled him out of the United States squad for the Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal against Haiti.
team_usa.summary: Reyna, 23, spent his last Borussia Dortmund years hurt and out of the lineup, and his move to Racing Club de Strasbourg in France put him back on the field week to week.
